mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE rises by more than 0.3pp for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines by more than 0.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 1.5% over two months signals a disinflationary tightening, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL < 1.5% for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls below 1.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth > 0.4% monthly for two months) and an increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% month-over-month signals strengthening household demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 0.4% AND HOUST > 5% MoM for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS grows > 0.4% and HOUST rises > 5% MoM for two months in an early-cycle environment.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for four consecutive months, combined with a decline in average hourly earnings growth (not directly observed but implied by labor market weakness), signals a deteriorating labor market that reduces consumer purchasing power and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 4.5% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (implied by RSAFS growth > 0.5% for three consecutive months) without a corresponding rise in consumption (GDPC1 flat) signals a savings glut that depresses demand for equities, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > 0.5% for 3 months AND GDPC1 flat
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS grows > 0.5% for three months and GDPC1 is flat.
